description: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents sign in to your accounts without ever seeing your passwords or one-time codes. When a supported agent reaches a sign-in page, it asks for a credential from your vault; you approve the request, and 1Password fills it straight into the site, so the secret never enters the model or its memory. You can see and manage which agents have access to what. It launched with integrations for agents such as Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work and dots, Meta's Muse and Grok Bot, and needs a 1Password plan.
pricing_detail: Included with 1Password plans

name: PhoneUse
description: PhoneUse gives AI agents phones of their own to operate. Agents get cloud Android phones that boot in seconds and scale to hundreds, or real retail iPhones and Androids in a San Francisco rack, tapped by a robot stylus, for apps that detect emulators, with real carrier numbers for SMS and 2FA codes. One MCP server with tools such as acquire, read screen, tap, type, swipe, open app and read SMS plugs into Claude, Cursor, Codex or Windsurf, and there is a Python SDK and REST API. On-demand cloud phones are billed per minute, with flat monthly prices for dedicated and real phones.
pricing_detail: Cloud phones $0.30 per minute on demand; dedicated and real phones monthly

name: Needle
description: Needle is an outbound engine built for AI agents to drive. You connect it to Claude, ChatGPT or Grok and describe who you want to reach in one prompt; it finds leads from LinkedIn, Instagram and Google Maps, enriches them with context for personal messages, and reaches out from your own connected accounts on whichever channel the lead uses, with sending limits built in. It works for sales, partnerships, hiring or fundraising outreach, and you can start for free.
pricing_detail: Free to start; paid plans

name: BAND
description: BAND is an interaction layer for teams running many AI agents alongside people. Agents and humans share one chat-like workspace where they coordinate tasks, exchange context and hand off work in real time, with governance over how agents communicate built in, instead of hand-wiring every handoff. BAND for Developers connects coding agents across your existing development tools so they can work together without you acting as their project manager.

name: UseIt Studio
description: UseIt Studio is an AI design agent for things you can hold. You describe what you want in a sentence, it asks the questions a designer would, and you refine any detail by pointing at it. Instead of a flat mockup you get a real, editable design file ready to print, cut and fold, with true dimensions, bleed and dielines, for pins, stickers, gift boxes, pop-up cards, packaging and brand kits. It runs in the browser, and a Windows desktop helper lets you call it up anywhere.
pricing_detail: Free to try; paid plans

name: Voxtral 3
description: Voxtral 3 is Mistral AI's voice agent stack: speech-to-text in 50+ languages with speaker labels and end-of-turn detection, expressive text-to-speech in 35+ languages, and a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit that handles listening, tool calls and speaking in one stream over SIP or WebRTC. You can use it through Mistral's API with EU, US or global endpoints, or deploy it yourself, and it is priced per minute of audio or per character.
pricing_detail: Transcription from $0.0035/min, TTS $13 per 1M characters, voice agent API from $0.04/min

name: Mercury 3
description: Mercury 3 is Inception's diffusion language model, which writes many tokens in parallel rather than one at a time, reaching over 1,000 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs with a 1M-token context, tool calling and structured outputs. It has an OpenAI-compatible API and is also offered on OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel, which makes it a fit for voice bots, support agents and browser agents where response speed matters. Pricing is per million input and output tokens.
pricing_detail: $0.20 / $0.70 per million input / output tokens

name: OmniRush
description: OmniRush is a desktop coding agent for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a terminal CLI as well. It works through the files of your own projects, reading code, making edits and running commands, and gives free access to frontier models from a model picker, with GPT 6 Astra as the default. Builds for each platform are published on its releases page.
pricing_detail: Free desktop app with free frontier-model access

name: Unreal Agent
description: Unreal Agent is an async-first agent harness from Unreal Labs, a team researching how to make agentic workflows efficient. The library handles inputs with stable IDs and deduplication, append-only sessions that can be forked, and a coordinator that manages each model turn and translates tool calls into operations. It ships with a cloud agent runner, a terminal UI and benchmark runners, under the MIT license.

name: MemoraX Code
description: MemoraX Code is a shared memory layer for coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Trae and DeepSeek Harness. It recalls prior engineering knowledge, captures lessons from finished work, keeps repository knowledge and architecture history up to date, and carries your procedures and preferences into new sessions, bringing back only the memory relevant to the task at hand. It needs Node.js 20 or later and is MIT licensed.

name: AOCI-CODE
description: AOCI-CODE keeps a persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase and database schema that your coding agent writes and a local MCP server governs. Agents in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode read the map once and know what each file is for, what it depends on and what must not break, instead of re-reading the repo on every task. It can index an existing codebase of up to about half a million lines and report how well it knows each area before taking over development.

name: OpenHarness
description: OpenHarness from Autonomous is a native command center for running coding agents side by side, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Devin, Amp and Copilot. It links your laptop, home server and GPU box into one window with a password instead of SSH keys or port forwarding, keeps code and keystrokes end-to-end encrypted through its relay, and is keyboard first. Agents keep working when you close it, and it extends beyond code to CAD, circuits, robots, games and music.

name: Wisp Science
description: Wisp Science is an open-source, local-first AI research workbench for scientists on Windows, macOS and Linux. Its agent searches the literature, runs persistent Python and R kernels on your laptop or remote servers, queries about 80 scientific databases and loads reusable skills, while keeping figures, runs, decisions and drafts together in one project. You bring your own OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic model, or drive Codex or Claude Code, and approval gates stay on by default.

name: Foreman
description: Foreman from ThruWire supervises coding agents with fast decision models. You give it a ticket, spec or bug report and it runs Codex, OpenCode, Hermes or LangChain's Deep Agents Code as workers, or attaches to supported sessions such as Pi, then independently judges whether the job meets the original requirements, whether the test evidence is enough and when verification or human input is needed. Extra checks can be configured for your workflow, and it is MIT licensed.

name: FableCut
description: FableCut is a Premiere-style video editor that runs entirely in the browser and exposes the whole timeline as one JSON document, covering media, clips, tracks, effects, keyframes and transitions. You can edit by hand or let an AI agent such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop cut the video over MCP or REST while the timeline updates live. It has no npm dependencies, starts with one node command and is MIT licensed.

name: Diagrid Catalyst MCP
description: The Diagrid Catalyst MCP server lets AI coding agents build and operate Dapr Workflows and Dapr durable agents on Diagrid Catalyst, the managed platform for long-running, fault-tolerant agent and workflow apps. Through it an agent can create and inspect workflows, check running instances and manage Catalyst resources from your MCP client. It is the official server from Diagrid, the company behind Dapr, and needs a Catalyst sign-in.

name: Cayu
description: Cayu is an open-source Python framework for building and running domain-specific, long-horizon agents on a durable runtime. Sessions survive restarts and redeploys from SQLite or Postgres stores, tool policies can require human approval before side effects, spend caps are checked before each model call, and timers, background tasks, subagents and forks cover longer multi-agent work. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

name: Inngest
description: Inngest is a durable workflow orchestration platform for running stateful step functions and AI workflows on serverless, servers or the edge. You write functions in TypeScript, Python or Go with automatic retries, queues, throttling and human-in-the-loop waits, and its AgentKit and AI inference steps let you build durable, long-running AI agents with tracing and evals. The server is source-available (SSPL, converting to Apache 2.0 later) and can be self-hosted, or you can use Inngest Cloud.
pricing_detail: Inngest Cloud: Free $0/mo (50k executions, 5 seats), Pro $99/mo, Business $499/mo, Enterprise custom (inngest.com/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Server is source-available (SSPL with delayed Apache 2.0) and self-hostable.

name: Windmill
description: Windmill is an open-source developer platform that turns scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, SQL and other languages into webhooks, workflows and internal UIs. Its flows include AI agent steps that call an LLM with your scripts as tools, support nested agents and MCP, and run on a fast self-hostable workflow engine. It positions itself as an open-source alternative to Retool and Temporal.
pricing_detail: Free and open-source Community Edition from $0/mo (self-hosted, unlimited executions, up to 10 SSO users); Enterprise from $120/mo; cloud and self-hosted paid plans (windmill.dev/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Core is AGPLv3, some enterprise features proprietary.

name: Kestra
description: Kestra is an open-source, event-driven orchestration and scheduling platform where workflows are declared in YAML or built in a no-code editor. It includes an AI Agent task that gives flows an LLM with memory and tools, supports nested agents and the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, and can expose any flow as a tool to external AI agents through its MCP server. It runs in the cloud, on-prem or air-gapped and is Apache 2.0 licensed.
pricing_detail: Open Source edition is free (Apache 2.0); Enterprise Edition and Kestra Cloud are annual subscriptions priced via sales, no public price (kestra.io/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026).

name: FloGPT
description: FloGPT is an AI chat and voice agent platform with a built-in AI CRM: embed a chat widget on your website, run AI phone agents around the clock, and handle chat, voice, email, SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook conversations from one inbox, all grounded in your own knowledge base.
pricing_detail: Freemium: free plan ($0/month plus usage for calls and SMS, 100 messages), then Starter $49/month, Growth $149/month or Professional $399/month, each plus usage for calls and SMS; prices as listed on its site

name: Reference to Video
description: Reference to Video turns product photos into 6-second AI ad clips for ecommerce and social: upload a product image, pick a shot style (showcase, lifestyle UGC, close-up detail or slow camera move) and an aspect ratio, and get a vertical, landscape or square video in 480p or 720p. Its reference mode treats the photo as a strict guide for tighter product fidelity and camera control.
pricing_detail: Paid: no free plan; one-time credit packs from $4.99 for 400 credits or $9.99 for 900 credits (valid 365 days), plus monthly and yearly plans; each 6-second clip costs 80-240 credits depending on mode and resolution; prices as listed on its site

name: Motion Transfer
description: Motion Transfer animates a character photo by copying the movement from a reference video: the photo sets the look while the clip drives gestures, expressions and body motion. Upload your own 4-30 second clip or pick a ready-made motion template, choose the model, resolution, length and aspect ratio in settings, see a credit estimate first, then preview and download the result. It also includes general AI image and video generation from one shared credit balance.
pricing_detail: Freemium: free Basic plan with one-time signup credits (the site banner advertises 60; the pricing page lists 18) and watermarked downloads; Starter $8.30/month billed yearly ($100/year, 2,400 credits), Pro $30/month billed yearly ($49.90 month-to-month), Business $49.90/month billed yearly; prices as listed on its site

name: Teebots
description: Teebots is a free desktop app that keeps a small team of AI bots on your own computer. Each bot can use a different model through your own API key, with requests going straight to the provider, and keeps its own private memory alongside a shared group memory. Put several bots in one group chat and @mention one to hand it a task, or let them pass steps to each other. Bots can work with files in their own folder, run commands, use skills including MCP and browse in their own browser, but they stop and wait for your approval before submitting or paying for anything. Scheduled daily or weekly jobs keep running from the menu bar. Chats, memory, files and logins stay local. Available for Mac (Apple silicon) now, with Windows and Linux coming soon.
pricing_detail: Free: the app costs nothing; model usage is billed to the API key you add. macOS (Apple silicon, v0.1.2) now; Windows and Linux coming soon

name: HaveTML
description: HaveTML lets AI agents publish what they make as a permanent share link. Ask Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to publish HTML, Markdown, JSON or YAML, and you get a sandboxed link anyone can open without logging in. Each link keeps its version history, supports comments, and can be set to private, unlisted or public.
pricing_detail: Free $0; Pro $6/mo or $60/yr; Team $20/mo

name: PeekPanda
description: PeekPanda is competitor research for iOS apps. Open any app to see the Meta ads it keeps paying for and how long each has run, the US App Store searches it ranks for, and which of its posts went viral. Use it in the web app, or add its MCP server so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can answer questions about any iOS competitor.
pricing_detail: Peek $59/mo; Panda $99/mo; $1 three-day trial

name: HireDov
description: HireDov is an AI sourcing agent. Describe what you need to buy and its agent, Dov, finds qualified suppliers, sends each a tailored request for quote in their own language, chases every reply and brings the quotes back to one dashboard to compare; first quotes usually arrive within a few days. You see the suppliers it finds before you pay.
pricing_detail: Pro $299/mo (100 credits); Business $799/mo (400 credits)

name: System One API
description: System One API is the hosted decision API behind TypeSafe Jev, with an open-source TypeScript SDK for AI agents. Where the TypeSafe Jev listing covers the decision model itself, this listing covers the developer API and console: send text or app context and get back a typed choice, a score or a yes/no probability for routing tools, ranking results and checking conditions, with API keys, call logs and credit use managed in one place.
pricing_detail: 100 free credits on sign-up; Starter $10 for 10,000 prepaid credits; no subscription

name: Financial Cents MCP
description: The Financial Cents MCP server connects an accounting, bookkeeping or tax firm's Financial Cents practice-management account to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and other MCP clients. Staff can ask about overdue work, unpaid invoices or missing client tax documents in plain English and have the assistant log time or create tasks, with each connection bound to one firm, your own permissions applied, writes confirmed in the client and deletes not offered at all. It is a hosted server signed in with OAuth and comes with the Scale plan.

name: Userpilot Agent Analytics
description: Userpilot Agent Analytics shows product teams how users actually get on with the AI agent inside their app. It reads the agent's conversations at scale and reports whether people got what they needed or left frustrated, so teams can see where the agent fails, which requests it can't handle and how agent use ties back to product engagement, alongside Userpilot's existing product analytics.

name: Tulimoa Memory
description: Tulimoa Memory is a hosted, shared memory store for AI agents and agent swarms. Agents write what they learn into it during the day; overnight a separate model sorts those notes into a knowledge graph with associative recall, and each agent starts the morning with a short briefing so it reads less and knows more. It is billed per call, with starting credit to try it.

name: Keboola MCP Server
description: Keboola's official MCP server lets AI assistants and coding agents work with a Keboola data project: browse storage tables and buckets, read and write SQL transformations, run and debug jobs and components, and build data flows from a chat. It can run locally or as Keboola's hosted remote server, with access scoped to the project token or OAuth sign-in you grant.

name: Speakeasy Gram
description: Gram is Speakeasy's open-source platform for building, hosting and governing MCP servers. Teams can turn APIs into curated MCP toolsets, host them, and manage which agents and people may use which servers from one control plane, with sign-in, access policies and usage visibility; its own MCP server lets an agent manage that setup directly.

name: SuprSend MCP
description: SuprSend's official hosted MCP server gives AI agents and coding assistants access to a SuprSend notification workspace. An agent can look up and manage users and lists, inspect and edit notification workflows and templates, and read delivery data across email, SMS, push, Slack and in-app inbox channels without leaving the chat or editor.
pricing_detail: Free plan $0/month (10k notifications/mo, no card); Essentials from $100/month billed annually; Business and Enterprise tiers

name: Edgegap MCP
description: Edgegap's official MCP server lets AI coding agents deploy and run multiplayer game servers on Edgegap's edge hosting network. From the editor, an agent can push server builds, start and stop deployments, check matchmaking and fleet status and read logs, so game developers can manage their online backend in plain language.

name: Jev
description: Jev is an open-source chat assistant for Android, Windows and macOS that reads the conversation on your screen, judges what the other person wants and whether a message looks risky, and drafts candidate replies for you. It fills in the reply box, but you always decide whether to send, so it helps with tricky messages without acting on its own.

name: Waku
description: Waku is a native desktop app that gathers your local coding agents in one place. It shows sessions from Amp, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok and Pi on a single timeline that stays entirely on your machine, so you can follow and switch between agent runs without juggling terminals.

name: Paritok
description: Paritok is a compression gateway that sits between a coding agent and its LLM. Using its own open-source 4B code-aware model, it shrinks tool output, files and conversation history on the fly without losing what the agent needs, which cuts token bills and lets agent sessions run longer before they hit context limits.

name: Rome OS
description: Rome is an open-source agent OS for recursive agents that compounds what they learn. Agents build their own tools, keep context and reuse capabilities across tasks instead of starting fresh each time, so a long-running assistant grows more capable the more it works.

name: TapQ
description: TapQ is an always-on voice layer for the coding and work agents you already run. You talk to Claude Code, Codex and others through your earbuds, interrupt them, steer the work and hear spoken updates, so you can supervise agents hands-free while away from the keyboard.

name: nanocode
description: nanocode is a small SDK for embedding frontier-model agents inside your own apps and tools. It provides the agent loop, tool calling and session handling for models such as Claude and GPT in a compact codebase, so developers can ship a capable embedded agent without adopting a heavy framework.

name: 0.security
description: 0 is an open, self-improving AI operating system for offensive security work. Its agents investigate code and binaries for vulnerabilities, test defenses, verify findings with working proofs and help fix the issues, and the team behind it publishes the advisories it has found in real open-source projects.

name: agent-manager
description: agent-manager is a terminal app built on tmux for running many AI coding agents at once. It shows live status for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Grok, Cursor and other sessions in a foldable project tree, adds a quick prompt bar, and has a diff reviewer whose line comments are sent straight back to the right agent, on macOS, Linux and Windows.

name: mu
description: mu is an open-source coding agent with a judgment kernel: a small, fast judge model makes the many routine decisions in each turn so the main model only gets the context it needs. It ships as a command-line tool and a desktop app and aims to keep coding sessions focused and cheap.

name: Streamkap MCP
description: Streamkap's official CLI and MCP server let AI agents manage real-time change-data-capture pipelines on Streamkap. An agent can create and edit sources, destinations, pipelines and transforms, check their status and troubleshoot lag, streaming database changes into warehouses and apps without clicking through the console.
pricing_detail: Free plan $0 (500 MB/month, MCP server included); paid plans priced by data volume

name: Agente Smart Documents
description: Agente Smart Documents turns a finished Word document into a reusable template your AI agent can fill. You upload an example, it builds the template, then ChatGPT or Codex, Claude, Grok Bot, Hermes or the web workspace asks only for the details that are missing and hands back a filled .docx with the original layout kept, for you to review before sending. A few documents are free each month, then a flat monthly fee per office.

name: CutBay
description: CutBay is a chat-based AI video agent that turns ideas, web links, documents, slides, spreadsheets and your own media into finished videos. You describe what you want and it drafts explainers, product demos, slideshows, animated charts, talking-head clips or YouTube Shorts, then lets you keep editing by chat, with add-ons such as B-roll and automatic subtitles.

name: only-cli
description: only-cli (oc) turns any website into a compact command-line view for AI agents. It distills a page into short text with numbered actions that agents like Claude Code can follow and click through, so agents browse the web using a small fraction of the tokens raw HTML or screenshots would take.

name: Vidmoat
description: Vidmoat is a hosted AI video editor you direct in chat. Describe the edit and its agent cuts dead air, adds word-synced captions, grades and reframes your footage on a real timeline, where you can review and change any cut by hand before rendering an MP4. It works in the browser, on Telegram (@vidmoat_bot) and over MCP (https://api.vidmoat.com/api/mcp, OAuth), so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can drive edits too.
pricing_detail: Hobby $0 (no card, 40 AI credits/mo, 720p with watermark); Creator $19/mo; Studio $49/mo; Team $29/seat/mo (min 3 seats); day passes from $2.99

name: SalesTouch
description: SalesTouch is a LinkedIn MCP server for AI agents. Connect Claude, Codex, ChatGPT or any remote MCP client to https://www.salestouch.io/api/mcp and your agent can find prospects, research people and companies, send invitations and messages, and handle follow-ups through 45 purpose-built LinkedIn tools instead of browser automation. Scoped OAuth, approvals for sensitive actions, daily limits, working hours and a human-paced action queue keep the account under control.
pricing_detail: $39/month or $389/year; 7-day free trial (card required, no charge before day 7); one LinkedIn account included

name: Vellm
description: Vellm turns photos of people and pets into short AI videos from ready-made templates. Pick one of 108 dance, funny, duo and pet templates built on ByteDance Seedance 2.5, upload your photos and it renders your own version, or start from a prompt in its Create Studio. A remote MCP server (https://api.vellm.app/mcp, OAuth sign-in) lets MCP-compatible AI apps create videos from your Vellm account.
pricing_detail: One-time credit packs from $4.49 (50 credits, one video) up to $39.99 (600 credits); monthly plans $20.99 (350 credits) and $41.99 (700 credits); templates cost 50-100 credits; no free trial

name: Crolytics
description: Crolytics is a managed, governed AI workspace for B2B marketing and go-to-market teams, hosted on Google Cloud. Its agents connect to your CMS, GA4, Search Console and knowledge base through custom MCP connectors, answer analytics questions in plain language, track how AI assistants cite your brand (GEO/AEO), and draft or update website pages behind human approval gates, with per-person permissions and a tamper-evident audit log. Teams use it from the Crolytics chat or inside their own Claude or ChatGPT account.
pricing_detail: Growth $5,000/month (managed and run for you, no per-seat or usage pricing); Enterprise custom; every plan starts with a free 2-week pilot after a scoping call

name: DIRI AI
description: DIRI AI is a voice role-play trainer for salespeople. You pick a situation, such as a price objection, an intro meeting, a cold call or a client who wants to leave, set the difficulty, and talk out loud with an AI customer that reacts to what you actually say rather than a fixed script. After each call you get an instant report with a transcript, the key moments highlighted and specific stronger wording to try next time, plus a history of your practice. Managers can use it to help new hires ramp up before real calls.
pricing_detail: Free €0 (no card): 1 voice call a day, up to 5 minutes, with a full report; Start €19.90/month (80 min), Plus €49.90/month (240 min), Pro €99.90/month (480 min); 7-day free trial on paid plans (card required)
good_for: sales teams practising calls, onboarding new reps, objection handling

name: Fileaify
description: Fileaify is a project workspace that plugs into the coding agent you already use, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf. You give the agent one URL (fileaify.com/agent) or the hosted MCP connector, approve its access, and it finds the project's documentation, architecture decisions, roadmap and known issues in each new conversation, so you don't have to explain the project again, even when you switch agents. Credentials stay in a vault: the agent can run approved actions with them without ever seeing the keys, sensitive actions need a human's approval, and paid tiers add a sandboxed executor where the agent can actually run work. The agent also writes its contributions back into the project docs, following your review rules. A live demo project lets you try it without installing anything.
pricing_detail: Free €0 (1 project, 5 services and secrets); Solo €4.90/month; Pro €14.90/month; Premium €39.90/month; Enterprise on request
good_for: coding agents that need project context, secrets kept out of prompts, human-approved access

name: img2threejs
description: img2threejs is an open-source agent workflow that looks at a reference image and rebuilds the object in it as a procedural Three.js model written purely in code. Each model goes through quality gates before it is accepted, comes out ready to animate, and is built in a token-efficient way, so a coding agent can turn photos or concept art into live 3D scenes without any mesh files.

name: Waggle
description: Waggle shows which files an AI agent actually opened before it answered. Instead of pasting whole documents between agents, it hands over short references that can be traced back to the source, so you can check whether an answer was grounded in what you gave the agent and send it back when it skipped the reading. It plugs into agent harnesses over MCP.

name: Strands Decider
description: Strands Decider is a small, fast decision model from Strands Labs for agent workflows. Rather than asking a full LLM every time, an agent can use it to choose between options or score something on a scale in a fraction of the time, with calibrated confidence so the workflow knows when to fall back to a bigger model.

name: Decionis
description: Decionis is an approval gateway for actions taken by AI agents. It sits in front of consequential API calls such as payments, price changes and orders, checks each one against your policy before it runs, and only lets it through with a single-use permit, keeping a signed record of every decision for audit.

name: Foremerge
description: Foremerge is an open-source coordination layer for teams of coding agents, built on top of Git. Each agent keeps its own worktree, but they share what they intend to change, claim the parts of the code they are working on and verify each other's change sets, so conflicting plans are caught before they turn into merge conflicts. It also works over MCP.

name: CodeAF
description: CodeAF is an open-source software factory from AgentField built to run on open models. It ships ready-made specialist agents you call with slash commands, one to build features like a senior developer, one to audit code for security issues and one to review GitHub pull requests, and spreads the work across a pool of models to balance cost and quality.

name: Kition
description: Kition is an open-source desktop office workspace with an AI agent built in. It combines documents, data tables and a whiteboard for design work in one app, and its tool-using agent can research the web, write and translate, organise records and produce editable brand assets, with visual workflows to chain the steps together.

name: BeefTV
description: BeefTV is an open-source, local-first desktop workspace for making AI video. On a free-form canvas you connect footage, images, generation models and agents into one flow, so you can go from an idea to finished clips without hopping between tools. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.

name: Aletheore
description: Aletheore audits code repositories and backs every finding with evidence. Its deterministic scanner looks for leaked secrets, vulnerable dependencies and dead code, it can watch live endpoints and draw architecture maps, and it reviews pull requests automatically through a GitHub Action. A built-in MCP server lets coding agents run the same audits.

name: Tura
description: Tura is an open-source agent runtime focused on cutting LLM spending. It manages the context an agent sends to the model so tasks use far fewer tokens, while keeping the finished results, execution evidence and benchmark scores auditable, which makes it aimed at teams running agents at scale.

name: PartMode
description: PartMode is open-source parametric 3D CAD that runs in the browser and is built to be driven by both people and AI agents. You can create multi-part designs and assemblies with lofts, sweeps and mates, browse a shared parts library, and export to STEP, STL, AMF or 3MF, while a command-line interface lets agents make permissioned changes. No account is needed.

name: Machinist
description: Machinist is an open-source software factory for coding agents. It runs agent jobs on your laptop, a virtual machine or a Kubernetes cluster, connects to GitHub so you can review the changes they make, and automates routine repository upkeep such as dependency bumps and fixes, with evals to check the results.

name: Concord
description: Concord lets coding agents message each other and work together in a shared workspace. Agents running in different tools or on different machines can hand off tasks, ask each other questions and review each other's code in real time through its MCP server, so a team of agents can coordinate without you copying messages between terminals.

name: JSON2Video MCP
description: The official JSON2Video MCP server lets AI agents produce videos through the JSON2Video API. An agent can render a movie from a JSON description, check on render status, validate the JSON before sending it and use ready-made templates, which makes it a fit for automated video production at scale; a free credit allowance is included.

name: ClicData MCP
description: ClicData's MCP server connects its data platform to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. You ask about churn, revenue or pipeline in plain language and get real analysis, live charts and full dashboards built from the governed business data you already keep in ClicData, which suits mid-sized teams without a data engineering group.

name: Shadeform
description: Shadeform is a marketplace for on-demand GPUs across more than 30 cloud providers, now with an official CLI and MCP server. AI agents can compare prices, launch and manage GPU instances and scale inference through one API, instead of you signing up to each cloud separately.

name: SecureAuth MCP Authority
description: SecureAuth MCP Authority is a security gateway for the MCP tool calls agents make. Every call is checked against the person the agent is acting for, using that person's own login and rules down to individual arguments, and each decision is logged so enterprises can see and control what their agents are allowed to do.

name: SimpleBackups MCP
description: The official SimpleBackups MCP server lets AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor and Codex manage your backups. From a chat you can check the status of server, database and storage backups, dig into failed runs and set up or automate backup jobs on your SimpleBackups account.

name: ChatAcademia
description: ChatAcademia is a set of AI research agents for academics. Its agents search many scholarly databases, pull insights out of papers and help with each step from forming an idea to drafting a publication, and a desktop app can work directly with the research documents on your own computer.

name: EnhanceWizard
description: EnhanceWizard is a browser-based AI image enhancer and upscaler that sharpens, unblurs, denoises and restores photos at original size, 2x or 4x. Its free browser tier processes images locally on your device up to 16 MP (8,192 px per side) with no sign-up, daily limit or watermark; optional cloud credits unlock Standard HD batch jobs up to 10 images and AI Retouch.
pricing_detail: Free $0 (no card, unlimited local browser processing up to 16 MP with no watermark); 50-credit pack $9 (one-time, valid 12 months); Monthly $12/month (100 credits/month)
good_for: upscaling and sharpening photos in the browser, restoring old or blurry photos, private local image enhancement

name: Pudding
description: Pudding is a desktop AI workspace from Teatak for macOS and Windows 11 that connects your own model API keys or local Ollama models with a built-in browser, file and command tools, a Studio for Markdown documents and typed tables, scheduled tasks, parallel subtask delegation and MCP plugins. Every tool call is shown in the conversation with per-project permission controls (Ask, Auto or Full access).
pricing_detail: Free desktop app for personal and commercial use (no account required; agent core Apache-2.0); model providers and external services charge separately
good_for: running models with a built-in browser and file tools, delegating parallel subtasks, local Ollama or BYOK desktop workflows

name: Orbi
description: Orbi is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) software factory for GitHub repositories. When you label a GitHub Issue ai-ready, Orbi implements it in an isolated worktree, opens and reviews pull requests in a separate AI review session that checks acceptance criteria and repairs failing tests, merges the exact reviewed commit SHA, and cuts a tagged GitHub Release when a human applies the ai-release label.
pricing_detail: Self-hosted: free and open source (AGPL-3.0 or Sustainable Use License, bring your own model); Cloud: 3 free merged deliveries (no card), Solo $24/month (400M tokens, 1 repo), Pro $66/month (1.2B tokens, 5 repos)
good_for: turning GitHub Issues into reviewed and merged pull requests, automated code review and repair, shipping tagged GitHub releases

name: Sora2 Hub
description: Sora2 Hub is a third-party multi-model web studio (not affiliated with OpenAI) for generating AI images and videos from text prompts or reference images. It brings together 10+ video and image models—including Sora 2, Veo 3.1, Kling AI, Runway, Hailuo 2.3, GPT-4o Image, Flux Kontext and Nano Banana Pro—alongside a prompt library and 2,000+ visual effects.
pricing_detail: Free starter access on sign-up; Basic $9.99/month ($7.99/month billed yearly, 1,000 credits); Pro $49.99/month ($39.99/month billed yearly, 5,000 credits); Ultra $99.99/month ($79.99/month billed yearly, 10,000 credits)
good_for: generating AI images and short videos from text or reference images, comparing multiple video and image models in one web studio

name: Massvai
description: Massvai is an AI full-stack app builder for Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Supabase. From a plain-language prompt or reference screenshot, its coding agent plans the architecture, writes exportable TypeScript code with a live HMR preview, wires Supabase authentication and database flows, syncs the repository to GitHub and deploys to Vercel.
pricing_detail: Free $0 (no card, 100 welcome credits, live preview, code export); Builder $25/month (1,500 credits/month, GitHub and Vercel deploy); Pro $49/month (4,000 credits/month, Supabase setup, version history); 20% off yearly
good_for: generating full-stack Next.js and TypeScript apps from a prompt, wiring Supabase auth and data, one-click GitHub and Vercel deployment

name: Images Upscale
description: Images Upscale is a browser-based AI image upscaler that uses cloud Real-ESRGAN models to enlarge JPG, PNG and WebP files 2x or 4x with modes tuned for photos, anime and illustrations, product shots and screenshots. It supports multi-image and ZIP batch uploads, watermark-free downloads, and companion tools for background removal, unblurring and alt-text generation.
pricing_detail: Free: 2 credits a day with watermark-free downloads; one-time credit packs (no subscription, credits never expire): Starter $9.99 (110 credits), Pro $19.99 (360 credits), Studio $49.99 (1,300 credits)
good_for: enlarging JPG, PNG and WebP images 2x or 4x in the browser, batch and ZIP image upscaling, product photos and anime illustrations

name: SiPhotoEditor
description: SiPhotoEditor is a browser-based AI photo editor where you upload a photo and describe the change in plain language—such as swapping the background, changing outfits, adjusting lighting or restyling a portrait—across eight editing models including Seedream 5 Flash and Nano Banana Pro, with side-by-side before-and-after comparison and multi-step follow-up edits.
pricing_detail: Paid (40 free trial credits with Google sign-in; edits cost 9–45 credits, failed edits refunded): one-time credit packs (never expire): Starter $9.90 (1,100 credits), Creator $29.90 (3,600 credits), Studio $79.90 (10,400 credits)
good_for: editing photos with plain-language instructions, swapping backgrounds and outfits, comparing before-and-after photo edits

name: SiGameGen
description: SiGameGen is an AI browser-game builder and arcade where a written prompt is turned into a playable single-file HTML5 game that you can refine by chat, play in private two-player rooms, share via link or download. Builds run on Fast (DeepSeek V4 Flash, 9 credits) or Pro (Kimi K2.7 Code, 45 credits), while playing, sharing and exporting games are free.
pricing_detail: Paid with credits (40 free credits on Google sign-in; Fast build 9 credits, Pro build 45 credits; failed builds refunded): first-game pack $9.90 (90 credits); one-time packs Starter $49.90 (1,800 credits), Creator $129.90 (5,000 credits), Studio $299.90 (12,500 credits)
good_for: prototyping playable HTML5 browser games from text prompts, refining game mechanics by chat, exporting single-file HTML games

name: Agenvas
description: Agenvas is an open-source (MIT), self-hosted infinite creative canvas where text, images, video, audio and AI agents work together on connected cards. Deployed with a single Docker Compose command, it connects to your own OpenAI-compatible endpoints, ComfyUI workflows and RunningHub apps, and gates agent media proposals behind human approval before generation runs.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT License, self-hosted via Docker Compose); you pay only for your own model API, ComfyUI or RunningHub usage
good_for: self-hosted multimodal creative canvases, combining text, image, video and audio cards with human-approved agent proposals, ComfyUI and RunningHub workflows

name: My Green Robot
description: My Green Robot is a consumer AI phone and email agent for Rhode Island homeowners that finds Google-rated local lawn care and landscaping companies, calls and emails up to three shops per request to ask your questions and book free on-site estimates, and brings back written quotes to compare side by side without phone tag.
pricing_detail: Free first request (no card, contacts 3 local pros, calls up to 5 min); Monthly $12/month (3 requests/month, up to 9 calls + emails); Yearly $119/year ($9.92/month, includes 2 free add-ons/month); add-ons from $1.99
good_for: getting and comparing local lawn care and landscaping quotes in Rhode Island, having an AI agent call and email contractors for on-site estimates

name: Zozo HQ
description: Zozo HQ is a coding-agent harness that turns dependency-ready issues from GitHub or matched Jira Cloud and Bitbucket Cloud into reviewable pull requests using isolated git worktrees, Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode via OpenRouter, and structured human clarification before anything merges.
pricing_detail: Free Local Stack ($0 on your own machine, bring your own model runtime); Hosted plans $40, $50 or $60/month before tax with a dedicated machine, no inference markup and a 14-day money-back guarantee
good_for: turning GitHub or Jira + Bitbucket issues into reviewable pull requests overnight with isolated worktrees and human clarification gates

name: Reverse Image Location (GeoSolver)
description: Reverse Image Location (GeoSolver) is an AI photo geolocation tool and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server (reverseimagelocation.com/mcp) that analyzes visible road signs, terrain, vegetation and architecture to suggest clue-by-clue location hypotheses for geography learning and public-place OSINT.
pricing_detail: Paid: Monthly $19.99/month or Yearly $69.99/year ($5.83/month) with a 7-day refund before paid use; separate EXIF viewer and geography guides are free
good_for: geolocating photos from visual clues in the browser or through a remote MCP server (geoguess and history tools)

name: MachGTM
description: MachGTM is an AI sales teammate for B2B software teams that builds an account brain from your website, finds and researches buyers with cited sources, maps account plans and writes tailored first messages.
pricing_detail: Design partners and early adopters. Terms agreed with each team.
good_for: B2B account research, buyer intent discovery and human-reviewed outbound first drafts

name: tta1
description: tta1 is a multilingual AI article-to-audio reader that fetches web articles, newsletters, X threads and X Articles—or accepts uploaded PDFs, Word documents and screenshots—strips menus and ads, optionally translates into your chosen language, and reads them aloud across 30 natural voices and 25 languages.
pricing_detail: Free ($0/month, no card, 1,000 words/month across 30 voices and 25 languages); Plus $6/month (25,000 words/month, PDF/Word/screenshot uploads, MP3 downloads); Pro $12/month (50,000 words/month); $5 per 25,000-word non-expiring top-up
good_for: listening to web articles, X threads, PDFs and screenshots read aloud or translated across 25 languages

name: CCC
description: CCC (Claude Command Center) is a free, source-available local dashboard for macOS, Linux and Windows that puts every Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and five other coding-agent sessions on one visual board, highlights which session needs your input, tracks token usage and lets sessions continue on $0 models when rate limits hit.
pricing_detail: Free and source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT, free for personal and commercial use, runs locally on localhost)
good_for: managing multiple local Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions on a single board and tracking which agent needs human attention

name: TokenRip
description: TokenRip is a shared multi-agent workspace that Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT, Grok and MCP-connected agents read and write together, storing versioned files, decisions and task feeds with one-line setup and human approval queues for outbound actions.
pricing_detail: Free ($0/month, unlimited workspaces and agents, 1 GB storage); optional Pro $20/month (10 GB storage) and Team $50/month
good_for: giving Claude, Codex, Cursor and Grok a shared workspace of versioned files, decisions and tasks with human approval gates

name: Agiloop
description: Agiloop is an AI-orchestrated software development platform that connects product requirements, architecture planning, AI coding, testing and production insights in one continuous loop, including a free Code Health and Readiness Assessment for existing repositories.
pricing_detail: Free planning, inspection and Code Health & Readiness Assessment; pay-as-you-go code generation at $0.25 per Agile story point with your own Anthropic/model API key or $1.00 per story point with Agiloop's key (no subscription)
good_for: evaluating existing AI-built codebases for production readiness and turning scoped Agile features into code with upfront per-story-point pricing

name: Clipkai
description: Clipkai is a browser-based AI video generator and photo editor that creates watermark-free videos from text prompts or reference photos across Seedance, Kling, Wan, Veo and MiniMax models, paired with 25+ one-click AI photo editing tools on non-expiring 1-year credit packs.
pricing_detail: One-time credit packs (valid 1 year, no subscription, commercial use included): Starter $9.90 (1,200 credits), Pro $29.90 (4,000 credits), Ultimate $69.90
good_for: generating short AI videos across Kling, Veo, Wan, Seedance and MiniMax or running one-click photo edits without a monthly subscription

name: Pangolinfo Amazon Data MCP
description: Pangolinfo Amazon Data MCP is a hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server (mcp.pangolinfo.com/mcp) and MIT-licensed stdio bridge that gives AI agents 19 read-only tools for live Amazon product search, reviews, seller catalogs, category metrics, WIPO design-patent checks and Google Trends research.
pricing_detail: Free tier includes 60 credits/month; paid Pangolinfo API plans available for higher volume (MIT open-source stdio bridge via npx pangolinfo-amazon-data-mcp)
good_for: giving Claude, Cursor and MCP-compatible agents live Amazon product, review, keyword, niche and WIPO patent research tools

name: imgs-ai
description: imgs-ai is an AI image and video creation platform with an official CLI and Agent Skill (imgs-ai-skill.md) that lets Skill-capable coding and personal agents quote live credit costs, request human approval, run text-to-image, reference-photo editing and video generation tasks, and download finished image or MP4 files.
pricing_detail: Pay-as-you-go credit packs ($0 monthly fee); Starter $49.99/month (1,800 monthly credits); Advanced $299.99/month (15,000 monthly credits, up to 5 concurrent tasks)
good_for: generating and editing AI images and videos from the web studio or directly inside an AI agent workflow via CLI and Agent Skill

name: Raydo Agent OS
description: The AI agent operating system for real work. Raydo gives autonomous agents a dedicated desktop workspace where they can browse the web, read and edit local files, run multi-step workflows across apps, and hand off tasks for human review. Built for founders, operators, and engineering teams that want background agents executing repeatable workflows with full step logs, sandboxing, and approval checkpoints.
pricing_detail: Free desktop workspace for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows; Raydo Cloud plans Plus $20/month (20,000 shared credits), Pro $100/month (100,000 credits) and Max $200/month (200,000 credits, 30% off annual), plus credit top-ups from $20
good_for: running desktop AI agents across live browser pages, local files and CLI tools with step logs, approval checkpoints and reusable deliverable records

name: Book Cover Generator
description: Book Cover Generator is a story-led AI book cover design studio for indie and self-publishing authors. Enter a book title, author name, genre and plain-language story summary to generate two distinct visual cover directions with integrated typography, refine the stronger concept with focused plain-language edits, and export watermark-free covers formatted for ebooks (1600×2560 JPG), Amazon KDP front covers (6×9 in at 300 DPI PNG), audiobooks (3000×3000 JPG) and HD previews.
pricing_detail: 20 free credits for new users (2 cover directions); one-time credit packs (no subscription): Basic $19 launch / $29 regular (100 credits, ~10 cover generations) and Pro $39 launch / $69 regular (500 credits, ~50 cover generations)
good_for: turning a book title, genre and story summary into two distinct, storefront-ready cover directions for ebooks, KDP front covers and audiobooks

name: NeverApply
description: NeverApply is an AI job-search agent and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server (neverapply.co/mcp) with 15 tools across job discovery, profile and resume preparation, and human-approved application submission. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Kiro or Grok via OAuth 2.1 with PKCE to search 919,000+ live roles, inspect match scores and quiet applications, tailor resumes, generate interview prep and submit applications on employer career sites after explicit per-job approval.
pricing_detail: Free ($0 forever, no card, 10 lifetime auto-applies, 5 matches/day preview, 50 MCP reads/day per client); Pro $29/month (150 apply credits/month, up to 5 Autopilot applies/day, Resume Studio, interview prep, 2,000 MCP reads/day); Max $49/month (450 apply credits/month, up to 15 Autopilot applies/day, automatic per-job resume tailoring)
good_for: searching matched jobs, tracking quiet applications, tailoring resumes and submitting human-approved job applications from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Grok via MCP

name: AI Music Mastering
description: AI Music Mastering is a browser-based automated audio mastering studio for finished recordings, DAW mixes and AI-generated songs. Upload WAV, MP3, FLAC or AIFF tracks up to 200 MB and 10 minutes long, audition eight sound profiles (Universal, Fire, Clarity, Tape, Natural, Spatial, Cinematic and Punch) with adjustable intensity, EQ and loudness-matched A/B previews for free, and export 24-bit WAV, 16-bit WAV or 320 kbps MP3 masters with a membership.
pricing_detail: Free preview (upload, 8 sound profiles, intensity & EQ controls, loudness-matched A/B original vs. master preview, latest 3 songs in history); Membership $9.90/month (24-bit & 16-bit WAV and 320 kbps MP3 downloads, reference-track mastering, full song history)
good_for: auditioning eight automated mastering profiles with loudness-matched A/B previews on recordings or AI-generated songs and exporting 24-bit/16-bit WAV or 320 kbps MP3 masters

name: Tanatasa Beauty MCP
description: Tanatasa Beauty MCP is a hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server (tanatasa-shopping 1.0.0 at tanatasa.sg/mcp), REST API and CLI for Tanatasa, a Singapore skincare and beauty store. Connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP-compatible assistant with no API key required to search authentic Korean and Japanese skincare and beauty products, inspect ingredients and usage details, verify live inventory and SGD prices, apply promo codes and create guest carts and 1-hour checkout links.
pricing_detail: Free (no API key or account required for catalog search, guest carts and checkout links; free standard delivery in Singapore on store purchases; MIT-licensed docs and @tanatasa/cli)
good_for: searching Singapore skincare and beauty products, checking live stock and SGD prices, and creating guest carts and checkout links from Claude, Cursor or any MCP client without an API key

name: LobsterMatch
description: LobsterMatch is a beta professional network for autonomous AI agents where operators register an agent with a public profile, match with complementary agents, coordinate tasks in signed 1:1 dialogs and sessions, and record completed collaborations on both profiles while keeping runtime credentials private.
pricing_detail: Free beta (public agent directory, onboarding skill v1.0.32 at lobstermatch.com/connect.md, private welcome inbox and signed notification webhooks)
good_for: giving autonomous AI agents a public profile, matching with counterpart agents for 1:1 sessions, and keeping verifiable collaboration records

name: KIWI
description: KIWI is an AI-native business workspace for freelancers, agencies and small teams featuring 24 named AI agents across operations, sales, marketing, finance and support. Sophia (Executive Assistant) is included on the free plan to triage email, schedule calendar events, prepare quotes and update the built-in CRM, while Premium unlocks 23 specialist agents, the Aukimi Creative Suite, video studio and social publishing with human approval before anything is sent.
pricing_detail: Free ($0/month, no card required: Sophia executive assistant, 30 AI credits/month, CRM, email & calendar, documents & spreadsheets, tasks); Premium $35/month (all 24 AI agents, full workspace, Aukimi Creative Suite, voice dictation & TTS, custom your-name.app.kiwi subdomain)
good_for: running back-office email, calendar, CRM, quotes, invoices and content from one workspace with Sophia and 23 specialist AI agents

name: Editara
description: Editara is a browser-based AI photo editor where you upload an image and describe what to change in plain English—removing objects or people, replacing or removing backgrounds, restoring and colorizing old photos, extending frames and upscaling—across eight selectable models including GPT Image 2, Nano Banana Pro and Seedream 5 Pro, with 12 free daily credits and watermark-free exports.
pricing_detail: Free: 12 credits to start with no sign-up (renews to 12 free credits/day when signed in, no watermarks); Monthly plans: Starter $9.99/mo (600 credits), Pro $29.99/mo (2,000 credits, commercial license), Ultimate $49.99/mo (3,400 credits), Max $79.99/mo (5,600 credits); non-expiring credit packs from $4.99 (150 credits)
good_for: removing objects, swapping backgrounds, restoring old photos and upscaling images in the browser with plain-language instructions and no watermark

name: Wenbu
description: Wenbu is a hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server (wenbu 1.5.0 at wenbu.app/mcp, listed in the official MCP Registry as app.wenbu/mcp) and web app for traditional Chinese cultural systems and reflection. Connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client with no API key required to call seven tools—calculate_bazi, cast_iching, draw_tarot, calculate_ziwei, search_library, read_library and get_daily_card—or run the MIT-licensed server locally.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT license; hosted Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at wenbu.app/mcp requires no API key or sign-up)
good_for: calculating BaZi and Zi Wei charts, casting I Ching hexagrams, drawing tarot spreads and searching traditional texts from Claude, Cursor or any MCP client without an API key

name: OMOPHub
description: OMOPHub is a hosted MCP server (mcp.omophub.com and npm @omophub/omophub-mcp, MIT) and REST API for OHDSI OMOP standardized medical vocabularies, giving AI agents and healthcare developers instant access to 11M+ clinical concepts and 63M+ relationships across SNOMED CT, ICD-10, LOINC, RxNorm and CPT without hosting a local vocabulary database.
pricing_detail: Free tier ($0, 100 requests/day, all standard OMOP vocabularies, Python/TypeScript SDKs and MIT-licensed MCP server); Pay-as-you-go from $10 credit pack ($0.001/request, credits never expire); Enterprise custom volume and SLA
good_for: searching, mapping and navigating SNOMED CT, ICD-10, LOINC and RxNorm medical terminology concepts inside Claude, Cursor or clinical AI agents via MCP

name: AutoCua
description: AutoCua is an open-source computer use agent that drives real desktop apps with mouse and keyboard on Windows, macOS and Linux, and also works in Chrome, Firefox and other browsers, in a real terminal and on an iPhone, iPad or iOS Simulator. It is built as a multi-agent harness you install with pip, so one agent can carry a task across the desktop, the web, the shell and a phone.

name: axuse
description: axuse gives AI agents browser and computer use through a single MCP server that plugs into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other MCP hosts. Instead of a screenshot loop it reads the DOM, the accessibility tree and Chrome DevTools, which makes actions faster and uses far fewer tokens, and it has zero dependencies, with desktop control on Windows, macOS (opt-in) and Linux.

name: Whirl
description: Whirl is an open-source AI chat app that lets you talk to every major model in one place, remembers what matters about you across conversations, and builds living documents and visualizations as you go. You can bring your own tools, so the assistant can do more than answer, and pick up any thread exactly where you left it.

name: BoardUI
description: BoardUI is a React design system for building agentic products and data-heavy dashboards, with 85 components and blocks (including chart cards), Tailwind CSS styling and fully editable source. The free set ships with a working AI chat app example, and Pro templates add ready-made layouts, so teams can put a polished interface on an agent quickly.

name: Elephant-Goldfish Model
description: Elephant-Goldfish Model is an open-source method and plugin from Google for spec-driven development with AI coding agents. A deep-context agent drafts the design, then fresh zero-context subagents stress-test that spec for gaps and wrong assumptions before any code is written, which catches problems that a single long-running agent tends to miss.

name: Open Analytics
description: Open Analytics is an open-source, cookieless alternative to Google Analytics with realtime visitors, funnels and revenue attribution from one lightweight script, and no consent banner needed. It includes an MCP server, so an AI agent can query your traffic and conversions directly, and you can self-host it or use the hosted version.

name: Doory
description: Doory is a free, open-source design platform in the browser for making social posts, slides, posters and logos, a self-hostable alternative to Canva. You can start designing right away without an account, using templates, text, shapes and images on a drag-and-drop canvas.

name: PiG
description: PiG is a faithful Go port of Pi, the open-source terminal coding agent, first developed at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. It keeps Pi's behaviour and extension model while shipping as a single fast Go binary, so you can run the same minimal, hackable coding agent without a Node.js runtime.

name: OpenClip
description: OpenClip is a free, open-source floating action bar for macOS that pops up when you select text. From it you can copy, calculate, transform text, run AI actions or trigger your own scripts and workflows, so quick jobs on any selection take one click instead of a trip to another app.

name: Gufo
description: Gufo is an open-source inference engine built for AMD Strix Halo machines that runs text, vision and speech models locally, with tuned kernels and published benchmarks for each supported model. It serves models through an API so local agents can use them, and image and video generation support is in progress.

name: Blaze MCP
description: The Blaze MCP server connects Blaze, the AI marketing platform for small businesses, to Claude and Codex. From a chat you can plan, create and schedule social posts, carousels, videos, blogs and newsletters in your brand's voice, then keep them on your Blaze content calendar.

name: GrowSurf MCP
description: GrowSurf's official MCP server lets AI assistants build and manage referral and affiliate programs in GrowSurf. An agent can set up a draft program, adjust rewards and pull participant and referral data for you to review, without clicking through the dashboard.

name: 3Dsellers MCP
description: 3Dsellers MCP is a hosted MCP server with more than 150 tools that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other AI assistants run eBay, Amazon, Walmart, Etsy and Shopify stores. Agents can manage listings, orders, messages and inventory without code or an eBay developer account.

name: Fly.io MCP
description: The Fly.io MCP server is one endpoint that connects your coding agent to Sprites, Fly.io's sandboxes for agents, and to your Fly.io apps. The agent can build and test freely in a Sprite, then move the result to a Fly Machine in production whenever you are ready, with the rest of Fly's cloud available along the way.

name: Tesla Wrap Generator
description: Tesla Wrap Generator is a browser-based AI design tool for Tesla's in-car Paint Shop where owners describe a wrap design in plain text or upload a reference photo, preview it on an interactive 3D Tesla (Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X or Cybertruck across 12 official UV templates), and download a Paint Shop-ready PNG template under 1 MB.
pricing_detail: Free (official Paint Shop UV templates across 12 variants, interactive 3D preview and <1 MB PNG fixer require no account; new accounts receive 10 free credits for AI wrap generation)
good_for: designing custom Tesla Paint Shop wraps from text prompts or reference photos, previewing panel alignment on a 3D Model 3, Model Y or Cybertruck, and exporting validated <1 MB UV PNG templates

description: B2B sales outreach platform with autonomous AI agents that research leads, draft personalized multi-channel outreach across email and SMS, check compliance before sending, and sync pipeline activity with HubSpot, Salesforce, Dynamics 365 and Airtable.

good_for: researching B2B leads, drafting compliance-checked email and SMS outreach sequences with human approval, and syncing replies to HubSpot or Salesforce
